questions.text:
You are a network engineer tasked with designing a communication network that connects 6 cities with the least possible cost. The cities are represented as nodes, and the cost of laying down cables between the cities is represented as the weighted edges between these nodes. The cities and costs are as follows:
1. City A to City B: 4  2. City A to City C: 2  3. City B to City C: 1  4. City B to City D: 5  5. City C to City D: 8  6. City C to City E: 10  7. City D to City E: 2  8. City D to City F: 6  9. City E to City F: 3

Task:
1. Draw the network graph representing the cities and the associated costs. [5 marks]
2. State the three steps involved in Kruskal's algorithm [3 marks]
3. Use Kruskal's algorithm to find the minimal spanning tree (MST) of this network. [10 marks]
4. Calculate the total minimum cost required to connect all the cities. [2 marks]

With reference to the assignment given on Knapsack and MST Algorithms in this Course, explain:
a) The working principles of the two Algorithms [10 marks]
b) Any two types of each of the Algorithms [5 marks]
c) One real-time application of each of the Algorithms [5 marks]

(a) What are NP- Complete Problems? Give two examples. [2 marks]
(b) What are the factors that make a problem NP – Complete in Computational Complexity Theory? [8 marks]
(c) Using the graph below, apply Kruskal Wallis Algorithm to obtain its Minimal Spanning Tree. Show your steps. [10 marks]
[Graph in the original paper: six unlabelled nodes joined by edges of weights 4, 4, 3, 3, 4, 2, 2 and 3.]

(a) Describe how Depth First Search (DFS) Algorithm works on a Graph. [3 marks]
(b) Using the following Graph, Illustrate how DFS Algorithm works. Show your steps. [7 marks]

(c) With real life examples, explain the following types of Graphs (No need of diagrams, just explain): (i) Bipartite Graphs (ii) Dense Graphs (iii) Complete Graphs (iv) Weighted Graphs (v) Undirected Graphs [2 marks each = 10]

"Maruwa" Tricycle drivers in UI usually carry three passengers from Main Gate to different locations on the Campus. Along the way, the driver can still pick more passengers to other destinations as some passengers drop off the vehicle.
(a) Draw a hypothetical graph showing some different links and nodes of different routes that a driver can take from Main Gate to the Department of Computer Science. [5 marks]
(b) Which of the standard algorithms learnt in this course can be suitably applied to help the drivers in covering all the routes in little time? Explain the reasons for your choice. [3 marks]
(c) Mention all the variants of the algorithm mentioned in (b) above. [3 marks]
(d) Describe with illustrative diagrams, how any of the algorithms could be applied to help the UI Drivers [7 marks]
(e) Give one limitation of your choice algorithm [2 marks]

(a) One of the works of compilers is to detect if arithmetic expressions are well-formed with respect to parenthesis (brackets) usage. Take for example, (a + b – [k * m] / j) is well-formed, but (a + b – (k * m] / j) is not. Write an algorithm to scan any arithmetic expression from left to right and indicate whether the expression is well-formed or not, using any suitable data structure. State the most likely Time Complexity for your algorithm [10 marks]
(b) The compiler finds postfix arithmetic expressions very easy to work with than infix ones. For instance, the infix arithmetic expression: a + b – c can be transformed to postfix to become ab+c- where the operator comes after the two operands. The compiler will then use the postfix expression for computation. Write an algorithm, using any suitable data structure to scan a postfix arithmetic expression from left to right and compute the value of the expression. State the most likely Time Complexity for your algorithm. [10 marks]

Amortized Analysis is a technique used in algorithm design to optimize some kinds of algorithms.
(a) Explain the meaning of Amortized Analysis. [2 marks]
(b) Explain the key idea behind amortized analysis. [2 marks]
(c) Give two (2) examples of data structures on whose algorithms Amortized Analysis can be applied. [2 marks]
(d) Briefly describe the three (3) methods for performing amortized analysis [6 marks]
(e) Describe how to perform Amortized Analysis on simple hash table insertions [8 marks]

(a) The performance of an algorithm and / or program is the amount of computer memory and time needed to run the algorithm or program. There are two measures of performance of algorithms. Discuss in detail the two measures. [7 marks]
(b) Explain the objectives behind designing algorithms. [3 marks]
(c) The classification of algorithms plays a crucial role in Computer Science. Explain any three reasons to support this assertion. [6 marks]
(d) Divide and Conquer is an algorithmic paradigm in which the problem is solved using the Divide, Conquer, and Combine strategy.
(i) Explain the underline terms. [3 marks]
(ii) Describe with simple diagram how Merge Sort follows the Divide and Conquer paradigm [2 marks]
(iii) The general solution to Merge Sort Time Complexity is T(n) = aT(n/b) + f(n). Explain what a, b, n and f(n) denote in the equation. [2 marks]
(iv) Give representative values to a, b, n and f(n) in the equation specified in d(iii) [2 marks]
(v) Use Master method to solve the time complexity for Merge Sort Algorithm [5 marks]

(a) The dynamic programming algorithm tries to find the shortest way to a solution when solving a problem. How? [5 marks]
(b) Give five (5) characteristics of dynamic programing Algorithms. [5 marks]
(c) The Floyd-Warshall method uses a technique of dynamic programming. Explain the problem solved by Floyd-Warshall method and how it solves it through dynamic programming technique [5 marks]

(a) Greedy algorithm is designed to achieve optimum solution for a given problem. Explain the general characteristics of a Greedy algorithm. [4 marks]
(b) Explain the steps involved in Greedy Algorithm [4 marks]
(c) Given the following graph, apply greedy approach to find the longest route in the graph and show that Greedy Algorithms are not always optimal in their solutions [7 marks]
